subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Cable Bundle Nobody Wanted
description: A quick win: understand The Cable Bundle Nobody Wanted.

hook.text: American cable bills averaged 200 dollars a month for 200 channels. Most households watched fewer than 20 of them.

buildup.text: The bundle worked for cable companies: force customers to pay for channels they don't watch to subsidize niche networks.

discovery.text: For years, consumers demanded a la carte pricing—paying only for channels they actually watched. The industry refused.

twist.text: Streaming services gave people what cable wouldn't: choice. Netflix cost 8 dollars a month versus 200 for cable.

climax.text: The cable bundle's collapse was self-inflicted.

punchline.text: Cable charged for 200 channels and lost to one app.

quiz.question: What consumer frustration drove the shift from cable to streaming?
options: Paying high prices for hundreds of channels they didn't watch
